{{see also|Hessian form of an elliptic curve}}
[[File:Symmetric Hesse pencil.svg|thumb|<p>Curves in the Hesse pencil of cubic curves <math>x^3+y^3+z^3=3kxyz</math>, as seen in a symmetric view of the projective plane in which the lines <math>x,y,z=0</math> form an equilateral triangle with the point 1:1:1 at its center, and the line <math>x+y+z=0</math> forms the line at infinity.</p>

<p>Different colors represent different curves in the pencil, corresponding to different choices of the parameter <math>k</math>:</p>
{{Bulleted list|1= The three black lines forming an equilateral triangle represent the degenerate case <math>xyz=0</math> corresponding to {{nowrap|<math>k=\infty</math>.}}
|2= The black point in the center is an isolated point from the degenerate case {{nowrap|<math>k=1</math>.}} It has as its roots the point 1:1:1 (shown, from a quadratic factor) and the line at infinity (not shown, from a linear factor).
|3=The blue and green curves represent choices of <math>k</math> with {{nowrap|<math>k>1</math>,}} forming two ovals in the real projective plane: a central oval inside the equilateral triangle, and an external oval with three inflection points at infinity, separating it into three real branches. The choices of <math>k</math> for the blue curves are (from lighter to darker) 36, 12, 6, 4, and 3. For the green curves, only the central oval is visible; their parameters are (from lighter to darker) 2, 1.5, 1.25, and 1.1
|4=The red curves represent choices of <math>k</math> with {{nowrap|<math>k<1</math>,}} having only a single oval with the same three inflection points and three real branches. Their choices of <math>k</math> are (from lighter to darker) –8, –2, –1, –0.5, 0.}}]]
In mathematics, the '''syzygetic pencil''' or '''Hesse pencil''', named for [[Otto Hesse]], is a [[Pencil (mathematics)|pencil]] (one-dimensional family) of [[cubic plane curve]]s in the [[complex projective plane]], defined by the equation
<math display=block>x^3+y^3+z^3 - \lambda xyz =0.</math>
Each curve in the pencil is determined by the parameter <math>\lambda</math> and consists of the points in the plane whose [[homogeneous coordinates]] <math>(x:y:z)</math> satisfy the equation.

The [[limit (mathematics)|limit]] of the curves when {{tmath|\lambda}} tends to infinity is the triplet of lines of equation {{tmath|1=xyz=0}}. So, it is generally not included in the pencil. For {{tmath|1=\lambda=3\zeta_3^j}} and {{tmath|0 \leq j \leq 2}}, where {{tmath|\zeta_3}} is a primitive third root of unity, the curve has a singular point at {{tmath|(\zeta_3^j:1:1)}} and is a union of three lines intersecting pairwise. Otherwise, the curve is non sigular and has {{tmath|(0:-1:1)}}, {{tmath|(1:0:-1)}}, and {{tmath|(1:-1:0)}} as [[inflexion point]]s. It is thus an [[elliptic curve]].

Each curve in the pencil passes through the nine points of the [[complex projective plane]] whose [[homogeneous coordinates]] are some permutation of 0, –1, and a [[cube root of unity]]. The Hesse pencil is thus the family of the cubic passing through these nine points. If one works over any field of [[characteristic of a field|characteristic]] different from three, this remains true except it may occur that these points are defined over an [[field extension|extension]] of the field. This does not work in characteristics 3, since, in this case, the points are not all distinct. 

The nine common points of the Hesse pencil are the [[inflection point]]s of each of the nonsingular cubic in the pencil. Any line that passes through at least two of these nine points passes through exactly three of them; the nine points and twelve lines through triples of points form the [[Hesse configuration]].

Given a nonsingular cubic plane curve, there Every elliptic curve is [[Birational geometry|birationally equivalent]] to a curve of the Hesse pencil; this is the [[Hessian form of an elliptic curve]]. However, the parameters (<math>\lambda,\mu</math>) of the Hessian form may belong to an [[extension field]] of the field of definition of the original curve.
